memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "In the tent of meeting, outside the curtain that shields the ark of the covenant law, Aaron and his sons are to keep the lamps burning before the Lord from evening till morning. This is to be a lasting ordinance among the Israelites for the generations to come." - Exodus 27:21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamps were to burn from evening till morning — through the whole night, every night, without fail. This was Aaron's ongoing responsibility, passed down through generations. Someone had to tend the flame in the dark hours, trimming wicks and adding oil while the camp slept.

The light burned precisely when it was darkest. That is when it was needed. And it did not stay lit on its own; it required attention, night after night, from people willing to do quiet, repeated work that nobody witnessed. Faithfulness in the dark hours kept the light alive.

Our own walk with God works much the same way. The flame is not maintained by dramatic experiences but by steady tending — daily prayer, regular Scripture, honest confession, ongoing dependence. Neglect the oil and the light gradually dims, often without our noticing until it is nearly out. Jesus told a parable about wise and foolish young women, and the difference between them was simply whether they had oil ready (Matt 25:1-13). Tend your lamp today. The dark hours are exactly when its light will matter most.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I faithfully tending the flame of my walk with God, or letting it dim?
What daily habit does God want me to be more consistent with?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my lamp burning through every season, especially the dark ones. Give me faithfulness in the quiet daily tending, so Your light in me does not grow dim. Amen.
